expectations.text: Uses an acceptance review task rather than a native gate issue
expectations.evidence: The response creates 'Docs lifecycle: acceptance review' as an explicit task with bd create, framed as a human acceptance gate with manual launcher + deterministic checks, wired via bd dep add dependencies rather than any native gate mechanism.

expectations.text: Uses numeric priorities like 0-4 or P0-P4 instead of high/medium/low
expectations.evidence: All bd create commands use --priority=2 or --priority=3. No high/medium/low strings appear anywhere in the plan.

expectations.text: Explains that needs-discussion work should use a needs:discussion label plus blocked status
expectations.evidence: The response explains a discussion-gate pattern (create a discussion issue, then block the execution task on it via bd dep add), but never mentions a 'needs:discussion' label. It uses dependency blocking but omits the label entirely.

expectations.text: Uses the bd create --body-file - pattern for structured issue bodies
expectations.evidence: All bd create calls use inline --description= strings. The --body-file - pattern for piping structured multi-line bodies is never mentioned or demonstrated.

expectations.text: Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution
expectations.evidence: bd ready and bd blocked are referenced only to explain their passive behavior ('invisible to bd ready until blockers closed', 'bd blocked will surface these'). Neither is recommended as a pre-execution check step a tasker should run before starting work.

claims.claim: Acceptance review task is created as a dependent task, not a native gate
claims.evidence: bd create --title='Docs lifecycle: acceptance review' with explicit bd dep add wiring to all upstream tasks.
--priority=2 and --priority=3 appear in all bd create commands; no textual priority labels used.

claims.claim: needs-discussion pattern explained via a dedicated discussion issue + bd dep add blocking
claims.evidence: Response shows creating a 'Discuss:' issue then wiring bd dep add <execution> <discussion>.

claims.claim: needs:discussion label is part of the pattern
claims.evidence: No label flag (--label or similar) is mentioned anywhere in the response.

claims.claim: --body-file - pattern used for structured issue bodies
claims.evidence: All bd create calls use inline --description= strings only.

uncertainties: Whether bd create supports a --label flag for needs:discussion in this project's beads version
needs_review: needs:discussion label support — response omits it entirely; skill should clarify whether it is a first-class flag or a freeform tag
bd create --body-file - pattern — not demonstrated despite the plan having multi-paragraph descriptions that would benefit from it
workarounds: Response substitutes inline --description= strings instead of --body-file -, which works but loses structured formatting for long bodies
Response substitutes dependency-only blocking instead of label+blocked status for needs-discussion tasks

eval_feedback.overall: 2/5 expectations met. The response correctly avoids native gate issues (uses an explicit acceptance review task) and correctly uses numeric priorities. It fails on three skill-specific conventions: the needs:discussion label is entirely absent (only dependency blocking is used), the --body-file - pattern is never shown despite the plan having rich multi-paragraph descriptions, and bd ready / bd blocked are not framed as pre-execution checks a tasker should actively run. The without_skill run is behaving as expected — it invents a reasonable workflow but misses the exact prescribed patterns.

suggestions.assertion: Explains that needs-discussion work should use a needs:discussion label plus blocked status
suggestions.reason: The skill should clarify that both a label AND a blocked-dependency are required — the label makes the reason machine-readable and visible in bd list filters; dependency alone is not sufficient per the expected convention.

suggestions.assertion: Uses the bd create --body-file - pattern for structured issue bodies
suggestions.reason: The eval prompt asks for a structured plan; the skill should explicitly demonstrate --body-file - with a heredoc for at least the epic and acceptance review task, since those have complex multi-line bodies.

suggestions.assertion: Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution
suggestions.reason: The expectation is about active workflow advice (run these commands before you start), not just passive description of their behavior. The grading criterion should be tightened to require an explicit 'before starting, run...' instruction.
